HKSJ.long: A small-sample variance correction for random-effects meta-analysis; gives wider, better-calibrated CIs when k is small.

REML.long: Default τ² estimator in metafor; less biased than DerSimonian-Laird for small k.

DL.long: Method-of-moments τ² estimator; classic but biased for small k. Avoid for k<10.

PM.long: Iterative method-of-moments τ² estimator; recommended over DL for small k.

I2.long: Proportion of total variance attributable to between-study heterogeneity. Not a magnitude — report τ² alongside.

tau2.long: Magnitude of heterogeneity on the same scale as the effect estimate.

PI.long: Plausible range for the true effect in a new study. Wider than the CI of the pooled estimate.

SMD.long: Effect size for continuous outcomes on different scales; Hedges' g recommended for k<20.

OR.long: Effect measure for binary outcomes; pool on the log scale (logOR).

RR.long: Effect measure for binary outcomes; pool on the log scale (logRR). Often preferred over OR for clinical interpretability.

HR.long: Effect measure for time-to-event outcomes; pool on the log scale.

RD.long: Effect measure for binary outcomes on the natural scale; complements ratio measures.

NMA.long: Pooled comparison of >2 interventions through a connected network of trials.

SUCRA.short: Surface under the cumulative ranking curve
SUCRA.long: Single-number summary of treatment ranking in NMA. Always pair with POTH and CrI of relative effects.

POTH.long: Calibration metric for SUCRA ranking. POTH < 0.5 means the hierarchy is non-informative.

GRADE.short: Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation
GRADE.long: Framework for rating certainty of evidence.

CINeMA.long: GRADE-aligned framework for rating certainty in NMA.

ROB-2.long: Domain-based tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials.

ROBINS-I.short: Risk of Bias in Non-randomised Studies of Interventions
ROBINS-I.long: Cochrane tool for non-randomised interventional studies.

QUADAS-2.short: Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2
QUADAS-2.long: Domain-based tool for risk of bias in diagnostic accuracy studies.

AMSTAR-2.short: A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2

PRISMA.short: Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
PRISMA.long: Reporting checklist + flow diagram for SRs/MAs.

RoB-ME.short: Risk of Bias due to Missing Evidence (Cochrane Ch.13, 2024+)
RoB-ME.long: Per-MA reporting-bias tool; replaces funnel/Egger as the verdict.

INSPECT-SR.long: Trustworthiness assessment for primary trials in an SR.

DOR.long: Single-number summary of diagnostic test accuracy; DOR = exp(μ₁ + μ₂) in a bivariate model.

SROC.long: Plot of sensitivity vs 1-specificity across DTA studies.

HSROC.long: Random-effects bivariate model for DTA. Use normal CDF (Φ), not logistic, for AUC.

TSA.long: Sequential boundary method for meta-analysis with monitoring boundaries (O'Brien-Fleming).

MID.long: Smallest change perceived as important by patients.

MCID.long: Synonymous with MID; emphasises clinical meaningfulness.

RMST.long: Time-to-event summary up to a fixed horizon τ*; pool differences, not ratios.

IPD.long: Trial-level participant-level dataset; gold standard for meta-analysis.

ITT.long: Analysis principle: analyse participants as randomised.

RCT.long: Experimental design with random allocation to interventions.

CrI.long: Bayesian equivalent of a confidence interval; interpretable as 'probability X falls in [a, b]'.

CI.long: Range of values consistent with the data at a stated coverage level.

ESS.long: MCMC diagnostic. ESS < 400 per parameter → unreliable CrI.

Rhat.long: MCMC convergence diagnostic. R̂ > 1.01 → do not interpret.

MAP.long: Bayesian prior derived from historical trials (Neuenschwander 2010).

PETPEESE.short: Precision-Effect Test + Precision-Effect Estimator with Standard Error
PETPEESE.long: Conditional small-study correction. PET first; if null rejected, switch to PEESE.

GOSH.long: All-subset sensitivity analysis. Random subsample for k>15.

Egger.long: Funnel-plot asymmetry test. Low power for k<10. Use radial version.

Peters.long: Funnel asymmetry test for binary outcomes; alternative to Egger.

TrimFill.long: Publication-bias visualisation. Sensitivity analysis only — never the primary result.

Bucher.long: Indirect treatment effect via a common comparator.

EBM.long: Clinical practice informed by best available research evidence.

PROSPERO.long: International prospective register of systematic reviews.

Cochrane.long: International network producing systematic reviews of healthcare interventions.

Schoenfeld.long: Proportional-hazards diagnostic. If rejected, single HR is misleading.

Guyot.long: Algorithm to reconstruct IPD from a Kaplan-Meier curve.

Fragility.long: Minimal number of event reassignments that flip a significant result. Modify ONE arm only.

NPD.long: Covariance-matrix pathology. Fix with nearPD() (Higham), not eigenvalue clamping.

Clopper.long: Exact binomial CI: qbeta(α/2, x, n-x+1).

Clopper-Pearson.long: Exact binomial CI: qbeta(α/2, x, n-x+1); the α/2 is correct.

TP.long: Diseased individuals correctly classified as test-positive (cell a of the 2×2 table).

FP.long: Non-diseased individuals incorrectly classified as test-positive (cell b).

FN.long: Diseased individuals incorrectly classified as test-negative (cell c).

TN.long: Non-diseased individuals correctly classified as test-negative (cell d).

Se.long: Se = TP/(TP+FN): proportion of truly diseased correctly identified as positive.

Sp.long: Sp = TN/(TN+FP): proportion of truly non-diseased correctly identified as negative.

FPR.long: FPR = 1 − Sp = FP/(FP+TN); the x-axis of the ROC/SROC plot.

ROC.long: Curve of sensitivity vs 1 − specificity across decision thresholds.

OLS.long: Linear-regression fit minimising squared residuals; used for the Moses-Littenberg SROC line.

DTA.long: Meta-analysis of test performance (sensitivity/specificity), not treatment effects.

DOR.long: DOR = (Se·Sp)/((1−Se)(1−Sp)) = LR+/LR−; a single global summary of test accuracy.

Bayesian.long: Inference framework combining prior beliefs with data via Bayes' theorem.

Frequentist.long: Inference framework based on long-run sampling distributions.

Funnel.long: Scatter of effect vs precision; visual aid for small-study effects.

Forest.long: Standard visualisation of effect estimates and CIs from each study + pooled.

Network.long: Graph of treatments connected by direct comparisons.

Indirect.long: Effect derived through a common comparator, not direct head-to-head.

MultiArm.long: Trial with >2 arms; NMA covariance for shared control = τ²/2.

Subgroup.long: Effect by participant characteristic. Pre-specify; treat post-hoc as hypothesis-generating.

Sensitivity.long: Re-run with alternative assumptions to check robustness.

Cumulative.long: MA updated as each new study arrives; for monitoring evidence accumulation.

Heterogeneity.long: Between-study variation in effect estimates. Quantify with τ², I², PI.

Bias.long: Systematic deviation from the truth. Distinguish from random error.

Power.long: Probability of detecting an effect when one exists.

Type1.long: False positive: rejecting a true null hypothesis.

Type2.long: False negative: failing to reject a false null hypothesis.

Effect.long: Quantitative summary of a relationship or difference.

MetaRegression.long: Regression of study-level effects on covariates.

Mixed.long: Random-effects MA + covariates; default in metafor.

Calibration.long: Agreement between predicted and observed risks.

Discrimination.long: Ability to rank cases above non-cases (AUC).

NetBenefit.long: Decision-analytic summary of clinical utility across thresholds.

QALY.long: Health-economic outcome combining length + quality of life.

ICER.long: Cost per QALY gained between interventions.
